decisions.reason: The name and professional summary are stated in the source; the listed negative claims also accurately reflect the explicit denials.
The role, employer, dates, personal project work, coworker training, and handbook are directly supported.

The project details and responsibilities are supported, but the source does not unambiguously establish that the tool was not also sold to external customers; it asks to distinguish operational use from a product sold externally.
The corrected six-run reconciliation metric, team attribution, personal contribution, coworkers’ changed habits, and exclusion of delivery speed are supported.
The source supports training 12 coworkers in two workshops, writing the handbook, and not supplying exact workshop dates.
The source identifies Python as a tool used to build Dispatch Loom and write its parser; the Data tools category is explicitly stated.
The source identifies SQL as a tool used to build Dispatch Loom and write its checks; the Data tools category is explicitly stated.
The source explicitly says PostgreSQL was used for the production database and places it in the Data tools category.
The source explicitly says Git was used for version control and places it in the Collaboration category.
The source supports personally training dispatch coworkers and places coworker training in the Collaboration category.
The degree, institution, and attendance dates are directly stated.
The source identifies the certificate as fictional, gives its date, and clarifies it was course completion rather than a professional license.
